tools.name: add_text
tools.description: Create point type at (x, y) (the first baseline), area type when width/height are given (`fit` autoHeight grows the frame to the text, shrinkText scales the text down to fit), or type in/on an existing path (`path` id + `mode` area|onPath; `pathEffect` rainbow|skew|3dRibbon|stairStep|gravity). Returns the text object id, with `overflow: true` when the text doesn't fit its frame or path (the lines past it aren't drawn: enlarge the frame, shrink the text or give `fit`).

color.description: Text colour (#rrggbb): "#rrggbb", "none", [r,g,b] (0..1), {"c","m","y","k"}, {"gray"}, or a full paint.setFill params object ({"gradient":…} / {"swatch":name})

fit.description: Area type: keep the frame (none), fit its height to the text (autoHeight) or scale overflowing text down (shrinkText)

fitMinPercent.description: shrinkText: the smallest scale in percent, 10 to 100 (default 50)

justify.description: Paragraph alignment (default auto: the start of the text's direction). Point type lines up on x: center centres each line on it, right ends it there

path.description: Existing path id to flow the text in (area) or along (onPath)

vertical.description: Vertical writing for point, area or path type (default false, horizontal), as text.create / text.createInPath

x.description: Baseline origin x (area type: left; point type: where the line starts, or its centre or end with justify center/right)

tools.name: answer_dialog
tools.description: Set fields of the desktop app's open dialog in order, then confirm (OK) or cancel it, as the control protocol's ui.dialog.set, ui.dialog.confirm and ui.dialog.cancel do. The app stores all the fields or none. When the app refuses the ui.dialog.set, for example because no dialog is open, the call is an error and the dialog is not confirmed or canceled. inspect_ui shows the open dialog and its fields (ui.dialog). After invoke_menu app.quit or file.close replies {"pending":"saveChanges"}: {action:"confirm"} saves, {set:[{field:"discard",value:true}],action:"confirm"} closes without saving, {action:"cancel"} cancels. Returns {dialog, result}: the dialog after the fields were set, and the reply to confirm or cancel. Desktop app only.

action.description: Then confirm (OK) or cancel the dialog

set.description: Fields to set, in order (one ui.dialog.set that sets all of them or none)

value.description: The field's new value (any JSON; default null)

tools.name: apply_effect
tools.description: Append a live effect (Effect menu) to the selection or `ids`. Omit `effect` to get the catalogue (ids, parameters, defaults). Examples: stylize.dropShadow {x, y, blur, opacity}, distort.roughen, warp.arc {bend}, path.offsetPath {offset}, pathfinder.add (on groups), blur.gaussian {radius}.

params.description: Effect parameters; missing keys take the dialog defaults

tools.name: command_batch
tools.description: Run steps in order; each edit is its own undo step, or with atomic:true the whole batch is one (named `label`, else after its first edit; `atomic` says which documents). A step's id is a command id, or draw_path / draw_shape with that tool's arguments as params (its result is the tool's: the new object's `id`). A param string that is exactly "$N.path" (N: 0-based step index) or "$last.path" takes that value from an earlier step's result, e.g. {"id":"$1.id"}; "$$" starts a literal "$". Returns completed, failed, results and created (the ids draw_path / draw_shape steps made, in order). Stops on the first error by default. At most 256 steps; kept step results total at most 8 MiB, past which the batch stops with the reason.

atomic.description: Make the batch's edits one undo step in the active document and in each document a step opens or creates; in a document open before the batch that a step switches to, each edit stays its own undo step

label.description: The undo step's name with atomic

tools.name: command_list
tools.description: Discover command ids, labels, parameter descriptions and enabled state. Returns an array. The whole catalogue is large: narrow it with filter (or query), menu, and brief. list_commands lists the same commands; it takes enabledOnly instead of enabled_only and returns {count, commands}.

brief.description: Leave out each command's params description (the bulk of the catalogue); run command_list with the id as filter to read it

filter.description: Case-insensitive id, label or menu substring

menu.description: Case-insensitive substring of the menu path, its levels joined with " > " (e.g. "Object", "Object > Path")

tools.name: command_run
tools.description: Run an engine command by id with its JSON params. Command parameters follow the registry's descriptions. run_command runs it the same way; it takes the id as command instead of id.

tools.name: create_graph
tools.description: Create a graph (graph tools) in the plot rectangle. Data as `csv` (first row: empty cell then series names; then one row per category: label, values…) or `series`/`categories`/`rows`. An empty CSV cell or a null in `rows` is a blank value (no column; lines break around it); a number in straight quotes is a label. Edit later with run_command graph.setData / graph.setType.

tools.name: doc_inspect
tools.description: Summary of the active document, including artboards, layer tree, selection and history. A node below full opacity reports `opacity` as a 0–1 fraction and `opacityPct` in the 0–100 % scale the drawing tools and object.setProps take: pass `opacityPct` back, never `opacity`. On a large document scope it: depth 0 for the layer skeleton, ids for just those nodes, kind for every node of one kind, limit/offset to page. inspect_document returns the same summary.

childLimit.description: Children shown per node (default all; a level that shows fewer reports childCount)

depth.description: Child levels of the layer tree to include (default all; 0 = top layers with counts)

ids.description: List just these nodes (any level) as `nodes` instead of the whole layer tree; an unknown id is an error

kind.description: List every node of this panel label (Layer, Group, Path, Type, Image, ...; ignores case) as `nodes`, each with its ancestor `path`; searches the subtrees of `ids` when given

limit.description: At most this many layers or nodes (the reply adds `total`)

tools.name: draw_path
tools.description: Create a path from points ([[x,y],…] or [{x,y,in?:[x,y],out?:[x,y]},…] with Bézier handles) or SVG path data `d`, then apply optional paint, stroke dash/cap/join, opacity, name and live effects. Omitted paint fields inherit the current new-art appearance (initially white fill and 1 pt black stroke). For a filled path without an outline, pass an explicit fill and stroke:"none". Returns the new object id.

d.description: SVG path data (alternative to points), e.g. "M0 0 L100 0 L50 80 Z"

dash.description: Dash and gap lengths in pt ([d, g, …]), or null for a solid stroke (stroke.set `dash`)

effects.description: Live effects applied in order, as apply_effect: [{effect: id (effect.list), params?: {…}}]

fill.description: Fill: "#rrggbb", "none", [r,g,b] (0..1), {"c","m","y","k"}, {"gray"}, or a full paint.setFill params object ({"gradient":…} / {"swatch":name})

opacity.description: Opacity in % (object.setProps `opacity`); doc_inspect reads it back as `opacityPct` (its `opacity` is a 0–1 fraction)

points.description: Anchors: [x,y] pairs or {x, y, in?, out?, smooth?} objects

stroke.description: Stroke: "#rrggbb", "none", [r,g,b] (0..1), {"c","m","y","k"}, {"gray"}, or a full paint.setFill params object ({"gradient":…} / {"swatch":name})

tools.name: draw_shape
tools.description: Create a live shape and apply optional paint. rectangle/ellipse: x, y, width, height (rectangle: radius = corner radius). polygon: cx, cy, radius, sides. star: cx, cy, radius1, radius2, points. line: x1, y1, x2, y2. Omitted paint fields inherit the current new-art appearance (initially white fill and 1 pt black stroke); lines start with no fill and a visible stroke. For a filled shape without an outline, pass an explicit fill and stroke:"none". Stroke dash/cap/join, opacity, name and live effects apply to the new shape as in draw_path. Returns the new object id.

dash.description: Dash and gap lengths in pt ([d, g, …]), or null for a solid stroke (stroke.set `dash`)

effects.description: Live effects applied in order, as apply_effect: [{effect: id (effect.list), params?: {…}}]

fill.description: Fill: "#rrggbb", "none", [r,g,b] (0..1), {"c","m","y","k"}, {"gray"}, or a full paint.setFill params object ({"gradient":…} / {"swatch":name})

opacity.description: Opacity in % (object.setProps `opacity`); doc_inspect reads it back as `opacityPct` (its `opacity` is a 0–1 fraction)

stroke.description: Stroke: "#rrggbb", "none", [r,g,b] (0..1), {"c","m","y","k"}, {"gray"}, or a full paint.setFill params object ({"gradient":…} / {"swatch":name})

tools.name: export
tools.description: Export the active document with the engine's document.export (the same bytes in the app and headless), in any format of the `format` enum: vectors (svg/svgz with the artboard as viewBox, eps, dxf, emf, wmf), pdf and ai (one page per artboard: all, or `artboard` / `range`; ai is the PDF-compatible .ai file that Save writes, which carries the document when every artboard is written in order), rasters (one rendered artboard: png, jpg, webp, gif, png8 as an indexed .png, tiff, bmp, tga, psd with its layers), txt (the stories, back to front), vectorcraft or template (a native copy or template; the document keeps its path). run_command document.formats lists each format's options. For SVG/SVGZ, top-level `outlineText: true` writes text as paths; DXF takes it too (its type is outlined anyway unless `preserve: editability`). PDF instead uses `options.advanced.outlineText: true`, default false (live text). `selection: true` exports only the selected objects, cropped to their bounds. Template layers are left out; live effects are kept (geometry baked, SVG filters for shadows/glows/blur). Without `path` the bytes come back as dataBase64.

artboard.description: 0-based artboard (default: the first; PDF and .ai default: all)

options.description: More format options, passed through (see run_command document.formats), e.g. {"quality": 80} for jpg or {"advanced": {"outlineText": true}} for PDF text as outlines (default false: live text)

outlineText.description: SVG/SVGZ: true writes text as outlines (viewable without the fonts). DXF takes it too (type outlined anyway unless preserve: editability). PDF uses options.advanced.outlineText instead (default false: live text)

range.description: 1-based artboards such as "1-3, 5" (PDF and .ai: one page each; SVG and SVGZ: one file each; EPS: one file each, after a central file of the whole document when there are two or more and art shows; rasters, DXF, EMF and WMF: one, or one file each with options.useArtboards: true)

selection.description: Export only the selection, cropped to it

tools.name: inspect_document
tools.description: Summary of the active document: artboards, layer tree (ids, names, kinds, bounds, fill/stroke; `opacity` as a 0–1 fraction and `opacityPct` in the 0–100 % scale the drawing tools take), selection, undo history, current tool and default paint. On a large document pass depth: 0 for the layer skeleton (truncated levels report childCount), then locate objects with run_command document.find and read them with document.node. doc_inspect returns the same summary.

childLimit.description: Children shown per node (default all; a level that shows fewer reports childCount)

depth.description: Child levels of the layer tree to include (default all; 0 = top layers with counts)

ids.description: List just these nodes (any level) as `nodes` instead of the whole layer tree; an unknown id is an error

kind.description: List every node of this panel label (Layer, Group, Path, Type, Image, ...; ignores case) as `nodes`, each with its ancestor `path`; searches the subtrees of `ids` when given

limit.description: At most this many layers or nodes (the reply adds `total`)

tools.name: inspect_ui
tools.description: UI state of the running desktop app: tool and options, panels, dialogs, view (zoom/center), window, documents, perf. Desktop app only. The same call as ui_inspect.

tools.name: invoke_menu
tools.description: Invoke a menu item by its command id (same ids as list_commands, including UI-only commands like view.zoomIn or window.* in the desktop app).

tools.name: list_commands
tools.description: List VectorCraft commands (id, label, menu path, shortcut, parameter description, enabled state). Every editing action is a command; run any of them with run_command. Coordinates are points in document space, y down, origin at the first artboard's top-left. command_list lists the same commands as a bare array and takes enabled_only.

brief.description: Leave out each command's params description (the bulk of the catalogue); run command_list with the id as filter to read it

enabledOnly.description: Only commands that can run right now

filter.description: Case-insensitive substring matched against id, label and menu path (e.g. "align", "Object")

menu.description: Case-insensitive substring of the menu path, its levels joined with " > " (e.g. "Object", "Object > Path")

tools.name: open_file
tools.description: Open a file as a new, active document: .vectorcraft, .drawcraft, .svg, .svgz, .pdf, .ai, .ait, .png, .pns, .jpg, .jpeg, .gif, .webp, .tif, .tiff, .bmp, .dib, .rle, .tga, .vda, .icb, .vst, .pcx, .pxr, .jpf, .jpx, .jp2, .j2k, .j2c, .jpc, .psd, .pdd, .psb, .vctemplate, .dxf, .emf, .wmf, .eps, .epsf, .ps, .af, .afdesign, .afpub (see run_command document.formats). Templates (.ait, native templates) open as a new untitled document. The reply's `warnings` say what didn't come in as it was (an EPS shown as its preview image says why its PostScript couldn't be read).

tools.name: open_panel
tools.description: Open a panel in the desktop app's dock by id (layers, swatches, stroke, align, pathfinder, transform, …; case-insensitive, display labels like "Layers" work too). Desktop app only.

tools.name: pathfinder
tools.description: Combine the selected (or `ids`) objects destructively, back to front: unite, minusFront, intersect, exclude, divide, trim, merge, crop, outline, minusBack. For a non-destructive version apply the pathfinder.* effect to a group.

tools.name: pointer_gesture
tools.description: Drive the active tool with mouse events in document coordinates, exactly like the mouse would (e.g. a rectangle drag: down at (100,100), drag to (200,150), up at (200,150)). Optionally selects `tool` first.

backquote.description: Default backquote held state for events: Selection and transform tool drags transform only pattern paint
Backquote held for this event: Selection and transform tool drags transform only pattern paint

holdMs.description: Milliseconds the pointer then holds still, button down (0..60000): Twirl, Pucker and Bloat keep applying

mods.description: Modifier keys held (cmd = Command on macOS / Ctrl elsewhere; alt = Option)

pressure.description: Pen pressure 0..1 (default 1): the Liquify tools' intensity with Use Pressure Pen on, and the pressure the Paintbrush records

rotation.description: Pen barrel rotation in degrees clockwise: the rotation the Paintbrush records for Rotation brushes

tiltX.description: Pen tilt in degrees −90..90, positive leaning right (document axes); with tiltY, the tilt the Paintbrush records for Tilt and Bearing brushes. One without the other is 0

tiltY.description: Pen tilt in degrees −90..90, positive leaning down the page

mods.description: Modifier keys held (cmd = Command on macOS / Ctrl elsewhere; alt = Option)

tool.description: Optional tool to select before the gesture

tools.name: press_key
tools.description: Send a key press with modifiers, e.g. {key:"Z", mods:{cmd:true}} (undo), {key:"Escape"}, {key:"Enter"}. In the desktop app it goes through the real keyboard path; headless, it runs the command or tool bound to that shortcut.

key.description: Key name: A–Z, 0–9, Enter, Escape, Delete, Backspace, Tab, Space, Left/Right/Up/Down, [ ]…

mods.description: Modifier keys held (cmd = Command on macOS / Ctrl elsewhere; alt = Option)

tools.name: redo
tools.description: Redo the last undone change (Edit → Redo): the change the last undo took back.

tools.name: render_preview
tools.description: Render an artboard (default the first) as inline PNG without changing the document. max_side defaults to 1024, limited to 1..4096.

traceViews.description: Draw Image Trace objects in the view set with imageTrace.setView (outlines, the source image…), as the app's window does; by default they draw their tracing result, as exports do

tools.name: run_command
tools.description: Execute any VectorCraft command by id with JSON params (see list_commands for ids and params). Examples: {"command":"object.group"}, {"command":"object.align","params":{"horizontal":"left"}}, {"command":"file.new","params":{"width":800,"height":600}}. Returns the command's result (e.g. {id} for creation commands). command_run runs it the same way and takes the id as id.

command.description: Command id, e.g. shape.rectangle, object.group, paint.setFill

tools.name: save_file
tools.description: Save the active document with the engine's document.save: by default to its own file in its own format (native .vectorcraft unless it was opened from or saved as SVG, PDF or a restorable .ai). With `path`, the extension picks the format: .vectorcraft, .vctemplate, .pdf, .svg, .svgz, .ai, .eps. Other formats are exports (see export). A native file is gzipped when `compress` is true (default: the useCompression preference, Preferences > File Handling > Use Compression); `version` writes it for an older VectorCraft and `preview` embeds a PNG of the first artboard. `options` carries the format's save options (see run_command document.formats); giving `compress`, `version` or `preview` both at the top level and in `options` with different values is an error. The reply's `format` says what was written and `warnings` what that format loses and each option given that the format doesn't read (such as `compress` for .svg). In the running app the call returns once the file is written, or with the error, even with Background Save on. When the save asks first (before replacing a file that opened with losses, or with a file dialog for an untitled document without `path`), the reply is `pending` or "cancelled" as before.

compress.description: Native files: gzip the file (default: the useCompression preference)

options.description: The format's save options, passed through (see run_command document.formats); default: as last saved

path.description: Destination; its extension picks the format (default: the document's own file)

preview.description: Native files: embed a PNG of the first artboard, at most 256 px (default false)

version.description: Native files: the format version to write (default: the current one; 1 and 2 are never compressed)

tools.name: screenshot
tools.description: Render the active artboard to PNG and return it as an image (optionally also saving it to `path`). With window:true (desktop app only) captures the whole app window instead, as ui_screenshot does; max_side then scales the returned image down (a file written to `path` keeps the full capture).

max_side.description: Window capture only: longest side of the returned image in pixels; a larger capture is scaled down to it (default: the full capture)

traceViews.description: Draw Image Trace objects in the view set with imageTrace.setView (outlines, the source image…), as the app's window does; by default they draw their tracing result, as exports do

window.description: Capture the app window (desktop app only)

tools.name: select_tool
tools.description: Switch the active tool (as clicking it in the Tools panel). Ids: selection, directSelection, groupSelection, pen, rectangle, roundedRectangle, ellipse, polygon, star, lineSegment, …

tools.name: set_paint
tools.description: Set fill, stroke and/or stroke weight on the selection (or `ids`) and as the default for new art. Returns {applied, objects}: `objects` counts the objects painted, as paint.setFill, paint.setStroke and stroke.set report them (the largest of their counts); when it is 0, a `note` says that only the default for new art changed.

fill.description: Fill: "#rrggbb", "none", [r,g,b] (0..1), {"c","m","y","k"}, {"gray"}, or a full paint.setFill params object ({"gradient":…} / {"swatch":name})

stroke.description: Stroke: "#rrggbb", "none", [r,g,b] (0..1), {"c","m","y","k"}, {"gray"}, or a full paint.setFill params object ({"gradient":…} / {"swatch":name})

tools.name: text_wrap
tools.description: Make the selected (or `ids`) objects wrap objects: area type below them in the same layer flows around them (offset in pt, invert = flow inside). `release: true` removes the wrap.

offset.description: Gap between text and object (default 6 pt)

tools.name: transform
tools.description: Move, rotate, scale, reflect or shear the selection (or `ids`); several may be combined and run in that order. Angles in degrees (counter-clockwise), scale in %. `origin` [x,y] defaults to the selection centre; `copy` transforms a copy.

tools.name: type_text
tools.description: Type text into the focused widget (text tool, dialog field). Desktop app only.

tools.name: ui_inspect
tools.description: Inspect the connected desktop interface; returns a tool error in headless mode. The same call as inspect_ui.

tools.name: ui_screenshot
tools.description: Capture the connected desktop window as inline PNG; requires a running desktop app. The same call as screenshot with window:true. max_side scales the returned image down to at most that many pixels on its longer side (1..4096; default: the full capture).

max_side.description: Window capture only: longest side of the returned image in pixels; a larger capture is scaled down to it (default: the full capture)

tools.name: undo
tools.description: Undo the last change (Edit → Undo). redo reapplies it.
